title: Length of Longest Subarray With at Most K Frequency
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. A subarray (a non-empty block of consecutive elements of `nums`) is called good when no value occurs in it more than `k` times. Return the length of the longest good subarray.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every subarray and counting its values costs O(n²). But goodness behaves well: if a window is good, every window inside it is good too. So for each right end we only need the smallest left end that keeps the window good, and that left end never moves backwards. A sliding window with a frequency map captures this in one pass.

## Approach

1. Keep `count`, a map from value to how often it appears in the window `nums[left..right]`. Start with `left = 0`, `best = 0`.
2. For each `right`, add `value = nums[right]` to `count`.
3. Only `value` can now exceed `k`. While it does, remove `nums[left]` from `count` and move `left` one step right.
4. The window is good again; update `best` with its length `right - left + 1`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2]`, `k = 2`. For `right = 0..5` every value appears at most twice, so the window grows to `[1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3]` and `best = 6`. At `right = 6` the value 1 appears a third time; dropping `nums[0] = 1` sets `left = 1` and the length stays 6. At `right = 7` the value 2 is too frequent; dropping `nums[1] = 2` gives `left = 2`, length 6 again. The answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index enters and leaves the window at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the frequency map in the worst case (all values distinct).

## Pitfalls

- Shrink with `while`, not `if`: several elements may have to leave before the newest value is back to `k`.
- Only the value just added can break the rule, so the loop only needs to check `count.get(value)`.
- Values reach 10^9, so use a map rather than an array indexed by value.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | how many times each value appears in the current window |
| `left`, `right` | first and last index of the window |
| `value` | the element just added at `right` |
| `best` | longest good window seen so far |

narration.2: count tracks how often each value occurs inside the current window.
narration.6: Grow the window by one element on the right each round.
narration.8: Record one more occurrence of the new value.
narration.9: Only the value just added can exceed k; while it does, the window is not good.
narration.10: Remove the leftmost element from the counts...
narration.11: ...and slide the left edge one step right.
narration.13: The window is good again; keep its length if it is the longest so far.
narration.15: After every right end has been tried, best is the longest good subarray.
